sources.quote: Noonan 1992:42 (verbatim as printed in Hyman 2010:309): "Primary stress i[n] Lango is invariably placed on the root syllable.... Where the root is longer than one syllable — only possible in nouns — the first vowel receives stress.... Stressed vowels in Lango are somewhat louder and slightly longer than unstressed vowels. The difference between stressed and unstressed vowels is not as pronounced as in English; instead, the relation between them is closer to that found in syllable timed languages
sources.note: The deciding passage is held only second-hand (Hyman 2010; StressTyp2), the two quoters differ in wording ('root syllable' vs 'root vowel'), and the reduplication and clitic clauses plus Noonan's own stressed-example list are unverified first-hand; two page images settle the record and let the grade field be filled.
